question: How have diffusion-model methods modified or used attention, at which structural level, for consistency, spatial control, temporal fusion, efficiency, and downstream multimodal tasks?

key_findings.claim: The survey's main organizing device separates the location of an attention intervention from the problem it is intended to solve.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 defines feature, map, function, weight, and application levels; Figure 4 and Table 1 cross those levels with four operational problem families—consistency enhancement, spatial control, temporal fusion, and computational efficiency—and list backbone, modality, and venue.

key_findings.claim: Consistency and control methods reuse attention in materially different ways rather than forming one interchangeable class.
key_findings.evidence: The survey distinguishes injecting self-attention keys/values or features, deriving masks and guidance losses from attention scores, aligning new conditions through separate cross-attention, directly replacing cross-attention maps, and composing selected local maps. It documents task-specific failure boundaries for layout, texture, identity, prompt alignment, and unseen content.

key_findings.claim: Temporal attention methods either insert explicitly temporal layers or align/reuse spatial features across frames, trading consistency against memory, long-video drift, and input-specific adaptation.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3.3 groups temporal attention injection separately from spatio-temporal feature alignment; application sections compare pretrained-image-model reuse, token fusion, motion prompts, and multimodal conditioning for video generation and editing.

key_findings.claim: The paper is a qualitative catalog rather than an empirical comparison or systematic review with reproducible selection criteria.
key_findings.evidence: It provides a 145-reference taxonomy and narrative application survey, but no database/query dates, inclusion/exclusion protocol, quality assessment, common benchmark table, code repository, or quantitative meta-analysis; performance statements inherit incomparable metrics from source papers.

method.core_idea: Decompose scaled dot-product attention into modifiable structural loci and classify diffusion methods both by intervention locus and application objective.
method.mechanism: The authors narratively review methods that change Q/K/V features, attention maps, attention functions, projection weights, or downstream uses of attention scores; then map them to generation, editing, perception, 3D, recommendation, and efficiency scenarios.
assumptions: A method's primary novelty can be assigned to one attention component even when it changes several model subsystems.
Architectures spanning U-Nets, latent diffusion, and diffusion transformers remain comparable under the same attention-level vocabulary.
Reported source-paper gains are sufficiently reliable for qualitative cross-task synthesis.

techniques.role: Labels whether a method modifies features, maps, functions, weights, or uses attention as an application signal.
Relates structural interventions to consistency, spatial control, temporal fusion, and efficiency.
Tracks image, text, video, and 3D combinations and the tasks in which each attention design is used.

limitations: Author-stated: attention-based editing remains task-specific, cross-attention map control struggles with prompt mismatch and unseen content, and efficient attention can lose quality or hardware occupancy.
Author-stated: discriminative use, interpretable attention, parameter-efficient adaptation, and native 3D attention remain underdeveloped.
Reviewer inference: a single-label taxonomy obscures hybrid systems that simultaneously alter maps, features, weights, and sampling guidance.
Reviewer inference: the survey freezes a fast-moving literature near April 2025 and gives no reproducible update or evidence-quality process.
failure_modes: Attention-map visualizations may look semantically meaningful without being faithful causal explanations of the denoiser.
Directly transferring spatial maps can preserve layout while blocking large geometry or action changes.
Linear, sparse, or token-pruned attention can reduce nominal complexity yet lose wall-clock gains or generation fidelity on real hardware.
reusable_insights: Describe diffusion-attention methods by both where they intervene and what invariant or control they seek.
Separate cross-modal alignment, spatial layout, identity/texture preservation, and temporal coherence instead of reporting one generic consistency score.
Efficiency reviews should distinguish algorithmic complexity, memory traffic, GPU occupancy, end-to-end latency, and quality loss.
open_questions: Can causal tests distinguish attention maps that control denoising from maps that merely correlate with generated content?
What standardized benchmark jointly measures edit fidelity, preservation, temporal consistency, and compute across attention interventions?
How should attention be defined and compared when diffusion transformers replace the U-Net/cross-attention template?

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Model-Based Image Editing: A Survey
competitive_landscape.difference: Huang et al. deeply taxonomy image editing and add the EditEval benchmark; the reviewed survey spans more modalities/tasks but contributes no benchmark and uses attention intervention level as its organizing axis.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient Diffusion Models: A Survey
competitive_landscape.difference: Shen et al. organize algorithm, system, and framework efficiency and maintain a paper repository; this review treats efficient attention as one branch beside control and temporal/semantic applications.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient Diffusion Models: A Comprehensive Survey from Principles to Practices
competitive_landscape.difference: Ma et al. cover architecture, training, inference, and deployment efficiency broadly; the reviewed work narrows to attention function/weight/application modifications and broadens to editing and multimodal alignment.

competitive_landscape.title: Prompt-to-Prompt Image Editing with Cross Attention Control
competitive_landscape.difference: Prompt-to-Prompt demonstrates direct cross-attention-map replacement for text-guided editing; the survey places it within a broader map-level family and explicitly identifies exact prompt alignment and unseen-region limitations.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: this is the first comprehensive survey to deconstruct attention modifications inside diffusion models into five structural levels while spanning multimodal applications. Reviewer inference after comparison: the two-axis taxonomy is a useful index and broader than image-editing reviews, but coverage overlaps multiple diffusion and efficiency surveys; without a systematic protocol, benchmark, or maintained artifact, novelty is primarily editorial organization.
reviewer_notes: Read all twenty densely typeset extracted pages, including the full taxonomy table, role/application sections, challenges, and references. No quantitative evaluation is attributed to this review itself. Competitors were checked against primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
